questions.q:
Write the chemical formula of each compound.
(a) aluminium oxide [1]
(b) ammonium carbonate [1]
(c) iron(II) hydroxide [1]
ms: do not allow incorrect cases, e.g. AL₂O₃ or Fe(oh)₂
questions.model:
(a) Al₂O₃ (Al³⁺ and O²⁻: two 3+ charges balance three 2− charges)
(b) (NH₄)₂CO₃ (two NH₄⁺ balance one CO₃²⁻)
(c) Fe(OH)₂ (one Fe²⁺ balances two OH⁻)
questions.tip: Put brackets round a group ion whenever you need more than one of it: (NH₄)₂, (OH)₂.

questions.q:
(a) A ball-and-stick model of a molecule shows 2 carbon atoms, 6 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom. Write the molecular formula of the molecule. [1]
(b) A diagram of part of an ionic lattice shows 6 lithium ions, Li⁺, and 3 oxide ions, O²⁻. Deduce the formula of the compound. [1]
questions.model:
(a) C₂H₆O
(b) The ratio Li⁺ : O²⁻ is 6 : 3 = 2 : 1, so the formula is Li₂O (two 1+ charges balance one 2− charge).
questions.tip: For an ionic lattice, simplify the ratio of ions — never write Li₆O₃.

questions.q:
(a) Aluminium burns in oxygen to form aluminium oxide. Write the balanced symbol equation. [1]
(b) When aqueous sodium hydroxide is added to aqueous copper(II) sulfate, a blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide forms. The other product is aqueous sodium sulfate.
Write the balanced symbol equation for this reaction, including state symbols. [2]
(c) Write the ionic equation, with state symbols, for the formation of the precipitate in (b). [2]
ms: (b) 2NaOH + CuSO₄ → Cu(OH)₂ + Na₂SO₄ (correct formulae and balanced)
(b) state symbols: NaOH(aq), CuSO₄(aq), Cu(OH)₂(s), Na₂SO₄(aq)
questions.tip: In an ionic equation leave out the spectator ions (here Na⁺ and SO₄²⁻); a precipitate is always (s).

questions.q:
Use the information to write balanced symbol equations, including state symbols.
(a) When solid sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃, is heated it decomposes into solid sodium carbonate, water vapour and carbon dioxide gas. [2]
(b) Magnesium burns in nitrogen gas to form solid magnesium nitride, which contains Mg²⁺ and N³⁻ ions. [2]
questions.tip: Work out the product formula from the ion charges first (3 × 2+ = 2 × 3−), then balance — never change a formula to balance.

questions.q:
Write ionic equations, with state symbols, for each of these reactions.
(a) Chlorine is bubbled into aqueous potassium bromide. Bromine and aqueous potassium chloride form. [2]
(b) Aqueous sodium hydroxide is added to aqueous iron(III) chloride. A red-brown precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide forms. [2]
(c) Zinc is added to dilute hydrochloric acid. Hydrogen and aqueous zinc chloride form. [2]
ms: (a) Cl₂(aq) or (g), Br⁻(aq), Cl⁻(aq), Br₂(aq) or (l)
questions.model:
(a) Cl₂(aq) + 2Br⁻(aq) → 2Cl⁻(aq) + Br₂(aq)
(b) Fe³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → Fe(OH)₃(s)
(c) Zn(s) + 2H⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + H₂(g)
questions.tip: Check that the charges balance as well as the atoms: in (c) the left has 2+ and the right has 2+.

questions.q:
A student adds solid copper(II) carbonate, CuCO₃, to dilute nitric acid, HNO₃. The mixture fizzes and a blue solution forms.
(a) Name all the products of the reaction. [1]
(b) Write the balanced symbol equation for the reaction, including state symbols. [3]
(c) The student then adds aqueous sodium carbonate to the blue solution. A precipitate of copper(II) carbonate forms. Write the ionic equation, with state symbols, for this reaction. [2]
ms: (a) copper(II) nitrate, water and carbon dioxide (all three)
(b) correct formulae: CuCO₃, HNO₃, Cu(NO₃)₂, H₂O, CO₂
(b) state symbols CuCO₃(s), HNO₃(aq), Cu(NO₃)₂(aq), H₂O(l), CO₂(g)
questions.model:
(a) Copper(II) nitrate, water and carbon dioxide.
(b) CuCO₃(s) + 2HNO₃(aq) → Cu(NO₃)₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)
(c) Cu²⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq) → CuCO₃(s)
questions.tip: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide: the fizzing is the CO₂.
